name: Arashiyama Bamboo
description: A path of living columns. The grove is planted and tended, not a wild accident.

name: Roof Phoenix
description: A bird on the gold pavilion roof. Look up after you decide if the gold is real.

name: Sacred Deer
description: Nara’s deer were messengers. Bowing is a learned trick. Food is not a toy.

name: Jizo
description: A small stone guardian by a road or temple path, often given a bib or hat.

name: Gion Festival
description: Kyoto’s summer festival. The tall floats are neighbourhood prayers on wheels.

name: Shrine or Temple
description: A torii and rope often mark a shrine. Incense and a cemetery often mark a temple.

name: Yokai
description: Old Japanese spirits. Fox, tanuki, kappa, tengu, oni — not Pokémon, though games borrowed the silhouettes.

name: Takoyaki
description: Octopus batter balls from a dimpled iron. Osaka food you eat standing up.

name: Okonomiyaki
description: A savoury pancake of cabbage and whatever you like. Hiroshima layers it; Osaka mixes it.

name: Kitchen of Japan
description: Osaka earned the nickname by feeding the country. The canal still sells the joke.

name: Dotonbori
description: A canal street of signs and theatres. Find the animals before the neon eats them.

name: Running Man
description: A sign big enough to steer a night walk. Osaka advertises by feeding you.

name: Manzai
description: Two-person comedy from Osaka: one straight face, one bounce.

name: Itsukushima Gate
description: A gate that stands in the sea when the tide is in, and on sand when it leaves.

name: Tengu
description: Long-nosed mountain spirits. Misen keeps their stories with the trees.

name: The Fire That Stays
description: A flame kept on Mount Misen. Confirm the local story when you stand there.

name: Momiji Manju
description: A maple-leaf bun from the island of maples.

name: Samurai Walls
description: Earthen walls and canals of a castle town the bombs missed.

name: Gold Leaf
description: Kanazawa still beats gold thinner than paper. Sometimes it even goes on ice cream.

name: Gassho-zukuri
description: Hands in prayer: a steep thatch roof built to shed snow and hide a silk attic.

name: Silk Attic
description: The upstairs of a gassho house was a workshop for worms, not only a bedroom.

name: Sarubobo
description: A faceless red doll from Hida. The missing face lets you put your own wish on it.

name: Festival Float
description: A street shrine on wheels, with carvings and hidden puppets.

name: Takayama Jinya
description: The shogunate’s mountain office. Paper, wood, and a long reach from Edo.

name: Hida Wood
description: Merchant streets built in timber because the mountains gave it freely.

name: Hida Beef
description: A mountain luxury. The live plate waits for a family photo.

name: Nakasendo
description: The inland road between Edo and Kyoto. Post towns still sell the walk.

name: Kosatsu
description: A government noticeboard at traveller height. Rules stood by the road.

name: Tokoname Ware
description: One of the Six Ancient Kilns. Clay pipes and teapots share the same earth.

name: Noborigama
description: A climbing kiln. Fire wants a slope so heat can walk uphill.

name: Tokonyan
description: Tokoname’s giant lucky cat. Find it in the street before you look at a photo.
